quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal to create space between your vehicle and the one ahead. This is safer than hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: On a hill, turn your wheels so your vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so a rear impact won't push you into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop completely. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if you take the right dose.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your driving. All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous. Know how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind resistance.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you and watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you and watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic behind and beside your vehicle before changing lanes. Make sure no vehicles are in your path.

questions.question: To turn quickly, place your hands:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the wheel.
On the top and bottom of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is safe and lets you turn quickly.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children, from any direction.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass before you proceed. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: Can you leave a vehicle's engine running after everyone has exited?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you will only be gone for a couple minutes.
Yes, if you will be gone for less than an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine and remove the key when you leave a vehicle. Always lock your vehicle when you leave it, even for a short time.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off wet surfaces and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that should be used with low beams.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: To prevent skidding on slippery surfaces, avoid slippery areas like ice patches, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. Dry, solid surfaces are safest to drive on.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has enough room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has enough room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: After the curve, there is a 35 mph speed limit.
Drive at least 35 mph through the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black writing. They tell you about conditions coming up ahead. Speed advisory plaques on these signs show the speed you should use.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the truck driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck so you cannot see the side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: You are being passed on both your right and left while driving in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On highways with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic on an interstate, use the right lane.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.
Always keep your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and look both ways before going.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways before going.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Drivers on both sides may pass.
The driver next to the broken line may pass.
The driver next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first begins. Oil and dirt on the road mix with water, creating a slick surface.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, stopped vehicles must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students have exited the bus.
The stop arm retracts.
The stop arm retracts and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm retracts and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: You must remain stopped while the school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm out. Only resume driving after the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus moves.

questions.question: You need to park where parking is not normally allowed. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Park where drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park where drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Make sure your parked vehicle does not become a hazard. Park in a location where drivers approaching from any direction can see it.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrian waves first.
Only if the pedestrian is not using a phone.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian cross. You may go only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning the road ahead for dangers. Do not stare only at the car directly in front of you. Check the road ahead and watch the vehicles around you.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road.
Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.
questions.explanation: Watch the sides, front, and back of your car. Good driving means knowing what is happening all around you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the posted speed limit when the signal turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: You are in a minor crash at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your car in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your car out of the traffic lane if possible.
Do not move your car for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car out of the traffic lane if possible.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries, move your car out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: Before making a U-turn, drivers should:

options.text: Honk to alert other drivers.
Make sure their car is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
Come to a complete stop in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure their car is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
questions.explanation: Before making a U-turn, check that your car can be seen for at least 500 feet in both directions.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off wet conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On freeways, watch for changes in traffic. Watch for signals from other drivers. Be ready for cars merging and changes in road conditions.
